POPULATION: this projection covers 167 declared ET-CC members and 84
declared in-population OC checks. That is the slice adjudicated so far,
and it is NOT the whole conformance picture: the full comparison is 281
ET-CC members and 173 in-denominator OC checks, of which 114 members and
89 checks are not_yet_adjudicated -- a third state, distinct from bucket
1 -- owned by the tickets the crosswalk's own `outside_the_population`
block names. A further 0 checks carry an edge without being declared by
any file, so they are counted in neither.

A count of zero in this view means zero WITHIN THAT SLICE. It does not
mean zero in the suite. As the declared population grows this projection
re-runs and fills.

EVERY FIGURE ABOVE IS INTERPOLATED from the crosswalk being projected;
none is written here. The [population_statement] guard refuses a
population figure that is not.

rows.claim: the DiscoverResult carries both mandatory discover fields — a supportedVersions list and a capabilities object
rows.evidence: discover_test.exs:24-29 — `assert map["supportedVersions"] == ["2026-07-28"]` and `assert is_map(map["capabilities"])`. Both of the check's disjuncts are asserted, so this edge is `:full` rather than `:partial`, and the second assertion is the one that makes it so: the OC predicate is `!g?.supportedVersions||!g?.capabilities`, and a unit asserting only the first would leave the second axis silent.

rows.claim: a server/discover request carrying no clientInfo is SERVED — HTTP 200 with a result, not an error
rows.evidence: streamable_http_stateless_test.exs:52-55 — `conn = post(opts(), rpc("server/discover", %{}))` sends `params` with NO `_meta` at all, and the unit then asserts `assert conn.status == 200` and reads `result` back with `assert r["supportedVersions"] == [@version]`. Both axes are covered: the status assertion is the HTTP-200 axis literally, and reading the `result` key is the no-error axis — `result(conn)` returns `nil` for an error body and the equality would redden. THE FIXTURES DIFFER AND THE DIFFERENCE IS STATED: the OC probe omits `clientInfo` ALONE (it sends protocolVersion and clientCapabilities), while this unit omits the whole `_meta`. For `server/discover` the two coincide — the unit's own name says `with no version gate`, and the check's own scenario places it on a method that applies none — so the claim entails the check's case rather than merely resembling it. On any OTHER method it would not, and this edge must not be read as licensing that.

rows.note: The only edge in this slice that is `:full` against a GREEN check on BOTH axes without a silent one to carry it. rows.claim: a server advertising the tools capability answers tools/list with a tools array
rows.evidence: streamable_http_stateless_test.exs:62-63 — `list = post(opts(), rpc("tools/list", with_meta(%{}))) |> result()` and `assert Enum.any?(list["tools"], &(&1["name"] == "whoami"))`: `tools/list` answers with a list, and it contains a real tool. The second axis is the OTHER arm of the check's `h.tools` CASE SPLIT — what a server that does NOT advertise the capability must do — and this SDK advertises it, so no unit of ours can take that branch. Silent, and silent for a reason that is a property of the check rather than a gap in the suite.

rows.claim: a notification type the filter did not request never reaches the stream
rows.evidence: subscriptions_stream_test.exs:348-356 — three unrequested pushes (`sink.("notifications/prompts/list_changed", %{})` among them), then one that IS opted in, and `assert decode(event)["method"] == "notifications/tools/list_changed"`: the NEXT event off the socket is the requested one, so none of the three arrived. The opted-in push is the positive control the OC check does not have — without it the assertion would pass just as well on a dead stream.

rows.claim: the SSE-framed error a refused listen produces carries the JSON-RPC id of the request that provoked it
rows.evidence: subscriptions_stream_test.exs:683-685 — `refusal = Jason.decode!(event.data)`, `assert refusal["id"] == "refuse-me"` and `assert refusal["error"]["code"] == -32_603`, against a request whose body set `"id" => "refuse-me"` at subscriptions_stream_test.exs:666 (`"id" => "refuse-me",`). The OC predicate is `e.id!==t` at the helper `u=(e,t)=>{e&&e.error&&e.id!==t&&r.push` — an error response whose id differs from the request's is the failure — and this is that comparison made by hand on a real response.

rows.note: Both halves of the check's guard are present in the unit and not merely in its outcome: the response IS an error (`refusal["error"]["code"]`), which is the helper's `e&&e.error` precondition, and the id is compared against the one the request carried.

rows.claim: a handler-side exit during teardown does not cost the error response its request id
rows.evidence: subscriptions_stream_test.exs:876-877 — `assert refusal["id"] == "exit-in-teardown"` and `assert refusal["error"]["code"] == -32_603` for a request that set `"id" => "exit-in-teardown"` at subscriptions_stream_test.exs:854 (`"id" => "exit-in-teardown",`). The same axis as the refusal edge, on the path where the SDK's own teardown faults — an instance the OC probe set cannot construct, because it has no way to make a conforming server's teardown exit.
